newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Savoy Hotel plans to take over New Star.
newsitem.headline: Savoy Hotel plans to take over New Star.

text.p: Seoul-based Savoy Hotel plans to buy a 51 percent stake of New Star Trading Co to take over the garment maker, a hotel official said on Friday.
If Savoy's move succeeded, it would be the nation's first hostile takeover of a listed company.
The official said Savoy already held a 24.70 percent stake of New Star and planned to buy the rest in the open market through tender offers.
He said the hotel wanted to buy the shares at between 40,000 won and 50,000 won against 38,000 won which they paid for the 24.70 percent stake.
New Star shares hit a 1997 high of 66,500 won, up 4,900.
"We plan to diversify business lines by acquiring the garment maker," he said.
But New Star announced a buy-back plan to defend against the corporate raider. It said it would buy five percent of its own common shares from April 21 to July 20.
The news sent New Star shares limit up in Friday's morning trading, brokers said.
"Investors believe they can make profits from the fight between Savoy Hotel and New Star Tading," said a Ssangyong Securities broker.
Analysts said they believed the hotel wanted to make a windfall from rocketing share prices rather than actually manage the company. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5647
